$comment: Single question list (implementation plan §1.3). Drives discovery/docs/client-questionnaire.md and discovery/docs/consultant-guide.md (npm run questionnaire:render), the discovery engine prompt mapping and the consultant interview. maps_to = JSON pointers into contracts/engagement.schema.json ('*' = every array item). feeds = gate:<id> | l_trigger:<id> | exit:<rule id> | app:<app signal id> from discovery/schema/offering.json. ask_when = "stop": asked only while an exit rule STOP is open. only_if = conditions on earlier answers without which the question does not apply in any mode (e.g. the mainland China questions). ask_if = conditions on earlier answers (any one is enough: equals, not_equals, in, includes_any, min, count_min, matches) that make a question feeding only app signals relevant in a quick interview. shopify = Shopify knowledge for the consultant (native features with minimum plan and docs, App Store category, app handles from discovery/schema/apps.json, extension points), never rendered in the client questionnaire. Enum options are read from the schema, never duplicated here.

sections.title: Business outcomes
sections.intro: What is broken before what to build. This section is the primary brief: every capability we scope must trace back to an answer here.

sections.title: Company, brand & Shopify
sections.intro: Store setup, Shopify plan, brand positioning and assets.

sections.title: Catalogue & products
sections.intro: Product model, variants, metafields, pricing and inventory.

sections.title: Markets & internationalisation
sections.intro: Shopify Markets, currencies, languages, tax and duties.

sections.title: Payments & checkout
sections.intro: Payment providers, PCI scope and checkout customisation.

sections.title: Shipping & fulfilment
sections.intro: How orders reach customers and come back: fulfilment, shipping, returns, cancellations, refunds and the post-purchase experience — and whether native Shopify (return and cancellation rules, self-serve returns, order status page, delivery dates) is enough or an app is needed.

sections.title: Customers, B2B & privacy
sections.intro: Customer accounts, B2B, loyalty, segmentation and personal-data obligations.

sections.title: Marketing & promotions
sections.intro: SEO, analytics, email, reviews, affiliates, discounts, campaigns and AI-driven commerce.

sections.title: Integrations & migration
sections.intro: Every system that exchanges data with the store, and what moves from the current platform.

sections.title: Design & experience
sections.intro: Design source, storefront approach, accessibility and performance.

sections.title: Delivery, governance & compliance
sections.intro: Timeline, decision-making, support, legal and project tooling.

questions.text: What is the single biggest thing preventing your ecommerce from growing right now?
How long has this been a problem, and what have you already tried to fix it?
If we solved only one thing in this engagement, what would have the highest business impact?
What is your current monthly ecommerce revenue (range and currency)?
What is your current conversion rate (%)?
Which product categories, markets or customer segments under-perform?
Is the main bottleneck acquisition (traffic), conversion (traffic doesn't buy) or retention (customers don't return)?
What share of revenue comes from each channel today (online store, retail stores, marketplaces, social commerce, wholesale / B2B, other)?
questions.help: Tells us whether retail, B2B and marketplace scope are in play.

questions.text: How many orders per month do you expect in the first year?
questions.help: Returns, tracking and fraud apps are priced by order volume.

questions.text: What manual work does your team do today that the platform should automate, and which processes break most often?
How many hours per week does the team spend on workarounds?
What does success look like in 12 months (revenue, new markets, channels, customer volume)?
Which KPIs will measure success? For each: metric, today's baseline, target, horizon in months.
What triggered this engagement — why Shopify, and why now?
If you are moving from another platform, what must not be lost in the transition?
What are you most unhappy with in the current store or set-up?
Which platform are you migrating from (or none — greenfield)?
questions.help: Shopify's Store Migration app imports products and customers from some platforms (e.g. WooCommerce, Wix, Square); other platforms use a migration app or the API.

questions.text: What is the approximate budget envelope for this project (range and currency)?
Is the priority to minimise upfront cost (apps and configuration), to own the solution (custom build), or a balance?
Is there a monthly ceiling for app subscriptions?
questions.help: Many needs are covered by Shopify's own apps (e.g. Subscriptions, Bundles, Search & Discovery, Translate & Adapt, Flow, Messaging). We check those first.

questions.text: Trading name and legal entity name (if different).
Country of incorporation / headquarters.
Industry and product vertical.
Is the business direct-to-consumer, B2B, or hybrid?
questions.help: B2B or hybrid brings the B2B and wholesale questions (§ 6.2).

questions.text: Current website URL.
Do you sell through more than one legal entity (e.g. one per country or region)? List them.
questions.help: Several selling entities in one store, or one store per entity, changes the store set-up.

native.plan_note: Needs Shopify Payments and the new Markets; otherwise expansion stores

questions.text: Where will you sell at launch?
questions.help: Online store, Shopify POS, Shop app, marketplaces, social channels, B2B, headless or app front ends, AI shopping agents.

native.feature: Sales channels (Online Store, POS, Shop, Marketplace Connect, Facebook & Instagram, Google & YouTube, TikTok)

questions.text: Is there an existing Shopify store?
Existing store URL, current Shopify plan and current theme.
Which Shopify plan will the new store run on (if already decided)?
questions.help: We recommend the plan once the requirements are known.

native.feature: Inventory purchase orders and transfers (Stocky retired 2026-08-31)

questions.text: How many people need their own Shopify admin login after go-live?
questions.help: Collaborator accounts and POS-only staff are not counted.

native.plan_note: Basic 0, Grow 5, Advanced 15, Plus unlimited; collaborators and POS-only staff not counted

questions.text: How would you describe the brand's positioning: value, mid-market, premium, luxury or enterprise?
questions.help: Positioning shapes the design depth and the solution approach.

questions.text: Is the brand identity finalised (logo, colour palette, typography)?
In which formats are brand assets available (SVG, PNG, Figma, guidelines PDF)?
Are there strict brand guidelines that must be followed?
What differentiates the brand — price, quality, exclusivity, community, sustainability?
Who are your top three online competitors?
Which stores (competitor or not) have a UX you want to reference?
How many active SKUs are in the catalogue (approximate)?
What is the maximum number of variant options on a product (e.g. size, colour, material = 3)?

questions.help: Shopify allows up to 2,048 variants per product.

native.plan_note: Apps must use the current GraphQL product APIs above 100 variants

questions.text: Are variants such as colours managed as separate products (own SKUs, images, URLs) that should appear as one product on the storefront?
questions.help: This is what Shopify calls combined listings.

questions.text: Which product types exist in the catalogue?
questions.help: Shopify Bundles creates fixed bundles and multipacks; mix-and-match bundles need an app.

questions.text: Will subscriptions run on Shopify Subscriptions (Shopify's app) or a third-party subscription app? Name the app if known.
questions.help: Shopify Subscriptions: customers skip, pause and cancel in their account; not with bundles or B2B.

native.plan_note: Not with bundles, B2B or draft orders; limited gateways

questions.text: If you sell bundles: what must they do?
questions.help: Shopify Bundles: up to 30 components; not with subscriptions or pre-orders; no nested bundles.

native.plan_note: Up to 30 components; not with subscriptions or pre-orders

questions.text: Which subscription features are needed?
For pre-orders, when is the customer charged?
questions.help: Pre-orders need a pre-order app; express checkouts (Shop Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay) are not available for pre-orders.

native.plan_note: Shopify Payments or PayPal Express only

questions.text: Do customers personalise products with choices that are not stock variants (engraving, file upload, paid add-ons, configurators)?
Roughly how many collections?
Are collections manual, rule-based (automated), or mixed?
Which product attributes go beyond Shopify's standard fields (technical specs, certifications, fit guides, ingredients)?
questions.help: Shopify stores extra attributes as metafields and metaobjects and uses the Standard Product Taxonomy for category attributes (filters, Google and Meta feeds). With a PIM, attributes come from the PIM.

native.plan_note: Metaobject definitions: 128 below Plus, 256 on Plus

questions.text: Where is catalogue data maintained today?
questions.help: Typical: products and content from the PIM; prices and inventory from the ERP.

questions.text: Which attributes should shoppers filter by on collection and search pages?
questions.help: Shopify Search & Discovery: up to 25 filters; no filters on collections over 5,000 products.

native.plan_note: Up to 25 filters; no filters on collections over 5,000 products

questions.text: Are there special prices for consumer groups (VIP or member prices)?
questions.help: Prices for business customers are covered in § 6.2. Consumer group prices use discounts for customer segments or an app.

native.plan_note: Up to 3 active catalogs below Plus

questions.text: Are there volume offers for shoppers (e.g. 3 for 2, tiered discounts)?
questions.help: Automatic discounts and buy X get Y cover most volume offers natively. Business volume pricing is covered in § 6.2.

questions.text: Do prices differ by market (not just currency conversion)?
questions.help: Shopify Markets supports percentage adjustments, fixed prices per product per country and price rounding.

questions.text: Where is the inventory source of truth — Shopify, ERP, WMS, other?
questions.help: With the ERP as source of truth, Shopify still needs stock per location.

questions.text: Are low-stock alerts needed?
questions.help: Shopify has no built-in low-stock alert; we set it up with Shopify Flow.

questions.text: What should happen when a product is out of stock?
questions.help: Continue selling (backorder) is native; back-in-stock alerts and pre-orders need apps.

native.feature: Continue selling when out of stock

questions.text: Which inventory tasks will your team do in Shopify?
questions.help: Purchase orders, transfers and stock adjustments are native in Shopify admin (Stocky is retired).

questions.text: Which markets (countries) go live at launch? For each: country code, checkout currency, languages, domain, and how prices are set (the store's base currency, auto-converted, a manual price list, or display only).
questions.help: List each country or group of countries that shares prices and currency. Mainland China is handled in a separate China discovery.

native.feature: Shopify Markets (no limit on country markets)

native.plan_note: 20 languages below Plus, 30 on Plus

questions.text: Which are the primary markets (one or more country or market codes)?
questions.help: The markets that lead revenue and launch priority, e.g. US and EU for a global brand.

questions.text: Which countries are planned in the next 12 months?
Operating model: one store with Shopify Markets, expansion stores, or hybrid?
questions.help: Expansion stores suit teams that run each region separately.

native.plan_note: Up to 9 expansion stores

questions.text: How should visitors reach their local market?
questions.help: Automatic redirection is native; EU visitors on EU country domains are not redirected automatically.

native.plan_note: The Geolocation app is retired

questions.text: Who is merchant of record for international orders?
questions.help: Self-managed Markets (the client registers and remits tax, Shopify Tax) or Shopify Managed Markets (Shopify is merchant of record).

native.feature: Managed Markets (Shopify as merchant of record)
native.plan_note: US and certain CA/UK stores; Shopify Payments; no B2B; subscriptions domestic only

questions.text: Should any market have its own theme content, section order, checkout or customer-account settings?
Are some products not allowed to be sold in certain markets (regulation, registration, licensing or distribution agreements)?
questions.help: List them in a note. In Shopify, products are excluded from the catalog of that market.

native.feature: Market catalogs: include or exclude products per market

questions.text: How will translation be handled?
questions.help: Translate & Adapt (Shopify's free app) auto-translates up to 2 languages; more languages need manual work or a translation app. Checkout is pre-translated.

native.plan_note: Auto-translates at most 2 languages; not policies

questions.text: Does any language need right-to-left layout?
Is SEO per language a priority?
What must be translated?
questions.help: Translate & Adapt does not auto-translate policies or URL handles.

questions.text: Should duties and import taxes be collected at checkout (DDP)?
questions.help: Duties and import taxes can be charged at checkout (DDP) or paid by the customer on delivery (DAP), chosen per country. Needs HS codes (and country of origin) on products; not combinable with tax overrides, manual tax rates or customer tax exemptions; DDP labels only with some carriers.

native.feature: Duties and import taxes at checkout (DDP or DAP per country)
native.plan_note: Plan not stated by Shopify; fee per order; not with tax overrides, manual rates or exemptions

questions.text: In which countries are you VAT-registered?
Do you sell into the US with state sales tax obligations?
Do products have HS codes and country of origin, and where do they come from?
Should prices include tax (VAT) in some markets and exclude it in others?
questions.help: Shopify can show tax-inclusive prices per market (dynamic tax display).

questions.text: Which tax service?
questions.help: Shopify Tax covers the US, EU, UK and Canada; since 2026-05-13 new stores selling in the EU, UK or Canada cannot use Basic Tax.

native.plan_note: Basic Tax closed to new EU, UK and Canada stores since 2026-05-13

questions.text: Do business customers buy tax-exempt (VAT number validation, reverse charge)?
questions.help: VAT ID validation at checkout is native.

questions.text: In which countries should duties and import taxes be collected at checkout (DDP)? In the others the customer pays on delivery (DAP).
questions.help: Countries, e.g. United States, United Kingdom, Switzerland. One choice per country: DDP and DAP can't both be offered in the same country. If you don't ship across borders, say so in a comment.

native.feature: DDP or DAP per country or region
native.plan_note: Not available for some destinations (e.g. Northern Ireland) or the Rest of world zone

questions.text: When you ship low-value parcels into these territories from outside them, are you registered to collect the import VAT or GST at checkout?
questions.help: Low-value parcels into the EU (IOSS), the UK, Switzerland, Norway (VOEC), Australia and New Zealand. Tick the schemes you are registered for.

native.feature: Low-value goods taxes (EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Australia, New Zealand)
native.plan_note: Registration needed; Shopify recommends DDP so orders above the threshold get duties calculated

native.feature: EU IOSS: collect VAT at checkout on low-value orders

questions.text: Do some products have reduced or zero tax rates, or tax exemptions, in any market (e.g. medicines, books, food, children's clothing)?
questions.help: Finance confirms the rates; Merkle does not give tax advice.

native.feature: Product categories for reduced rates and exemptions (Shopify Tax: US, EU, UK)
Product tax overrides per country or state (manual collections)
native.plan_note: Ignored where duties are collected at checkout

questions.text: Who issues invoices to customers?
questions.help: Shopify can generate VAT invoices for EU and UK orders (shown on the order status page, not emailed, not for orders with duties). The free Order Printer app prints invoices from templates. Invoices can also come from the ERP or an invoicing app.

native.feature: VAT invoices for EU and UK orders
native.plan_note: Shopify Tax; not emailed; not for orders with duties; Portugal not supported

questions.text: Which electronic invoicing (e-invoicing) obligations apply to your sales?
questions.help: For example Peppol, XRechnung or ZUGFeRD (Germany), Factur-X (France), SdI (Italy), KSeF (Poland) or VeriFactu (Spain). Shopify has no built-in e-invoicing: it comes from the ERP or an invoicing app.

native.feature: VAT invoices for EU and UK orders (not e-invoicing)

questions.text: Do you want to sell to mainland China cross-border (from outside China) or onshore, behind the Great Firewall?
questions.help: Onshore selling needs a PRC entity, an ICP filing or licence and hosting in China.

native.feature: Shopify in China: Shopify's servers are not located in mainland China

questions.text: Which channels for mainland China?
questions.help: Cross-border marketplaces (Tmall Global, JD Worldwide, Douyin Global, RED), a WeChat mini-program, your own site, or a Hong Kong store shipping to the mainland.

questions.text: Do you have a legal entity in mainland China?
questions.help: Needed for an ICP filing or licence and for onshore hosting.

questions.text: Do you have a Hong Kong or other overseas entity that can sell cross-border, and are your trademarks registered in China?
questions.help: Cross-border marketplaces require both.

questions.text: ICP status for a China website?
questions.help: Your PRC counsel confirms whether a filing is enough or a commercial ICP licence is needed.

questions.text: What is Shopify's role for mainland China?
questions.help: Shopify can stay the global master for products, inventory and orders while China sells through local channels.

native.feature: Shopify in China: Shopify's servers are not located in mainland China

questions.text: How will goods enter China: bonded warehouse (1210), direct mail (9610), general trade, or personal parcels?
questions.help: Cross-border channels have per-order and yearly limits per consumer.

questions.text: Are your products on China's cross-border e-commerce positive list?
How are your products classified in China?
questions.help: Whitening, sunscreen and anti-hair-loss products are special cosmetics; medicines are not cross-border goods.

questions.text: Registration or filing status with China's medical products administration (NMPA)?
questions.help: General trade needs registration or filing; cross-border channels are exempt for goods on the positive list.

questions.text: Do product claims need a review for China (medical, cosmeceutical or treatment claims)?
questions.help: China does not allow cosmeceutical or medical claims for cosmetics.

questions.text: How will mainland customers pay?
questions.help: Inside the marketplace, Alipay and WeChat Pay through a Hong Kong Shopify Payments account (early access), a cross-border wallet provider, or domestic merchant accounts (PRC entity).

Hong Kong SAR Shopify Payments account; early access

questions.text: How many mainland China customers do you expect per year?
questions.help: China's personal information law sets different data-export obligations by volume.

questions.text: Do you have a representative in China for personal information protection (PIPL)?
questions.help: Required when an offshore business targets consumers in China.

questions.text: Where will China customer data (CRM, email, analytics) be stored?
Must scripts blocked in China (Google Fonts, Google Analytics, reCAPTCHA, Meta pixels, YouTube) be replaced?

questions.text: Which marketing channels for China?
Who provides Chinese-language customer service?
Do you work with a local partner or trade partner for China? Name it.
Target launch date for mainland China.

questions.text: Which local payment methods are required?

questions.text: Which express checkouts are required?
questions.help: B2B checkout and pre-orders do not support express checkouts.

questions.text: Must payment methods be hidden, renamed or reordered by market, customer type or cart?

questions.help: Shopify checkout is customised with the checkout editor and Checkout Extensibility (blocks, fields, logic via Functions). A fully custom checkout UI is not possible on Shopify.

Checkout UI extensions on information, shipping and payment steps; Checkout Branding API

Which 3PL provider?

questions.help: Shopify's order routing rules: minimise split shipments, stay within the market, closest location, ranked locations, location metafields. Anything else needs a custom routing function or the ERP / OMS.

questions.text: Which carriers do you use?
How are shipping rates calculated?
questions.help: Flat, weight or price based, free above a threshold, live carrier rates, or rates from an app.

native.plan_note: Add-on on Grow

questions.text: Are there product-specific shipping rules (heavy, hazardous, temperature-controlled)?
Which countries do you not ship to?
Free-shipping thresholds per market (market, threshold, currency, which rates).

How many days do customers have to return an order?
What share of orders is returned today (%)?

questions.text: How do customers send items back: prepaid label, QR code drop-off, their own shipment, or mixed?

questions.text: Which shipping rules differ for B2B buyers?
questions.help: By default B2B and consumer buyers see the same shipping methods. Different options need Checkout Blocks, an app or a delivery customization function; orders can also be submitted as drafts so shipping is quoted before payment.

native.feature: B2B shipping methods (same as consumers by default; customise per buyer)
native.plan_note: Custom apps with Shopify Functions need Plus; public apps with functions work on any plan

native.feature: Submit B2B orders as drafts for review

questions.text: Which customer tags drive custom logic today (pricing, access, discounts)?

Do you collect sensitive personal data (health, age, biometric, financial)?
questions.help: Sensitive data needs a data protection impact assessment and legal sign-off.

questions.text: Must data-access or deletion requests reach systems beyond Shopify (ERP, email platform) or run without staff involvement?
questions.help: Shopify handles export and erasure requests in admin; other systems or automation need extra design and legal sign-off.

questions.text: Do US state privacy laws require a 'Do not sell or share my personal information' page?
questions.help: A native opt-out page honours Global Privacy Control.

questions.help: Shopify Catalog and agentic channels (Spring '26).

questions.text: Which analytics platforms do you use (GA4, Adobe, other)?
Is server-side tracking needed?
questions.help: Shopify's customer events track storefront and checkout with consent; the Facebook & Instagram and Google & YouTube apps send server-side events. Anything beyond needs a tracking app. Server-side events can share customer data with ad platforms (PII gate).

questions.text: Which advertising pixels are needed (Meta, TikTok, Pinterest, Google Ads)?

native.plan_note: AT, CA, DK, FI, IT, LU, PL, PT, SE, UK, US; Spain paused since 2026-09-15

questions.text: Do you send WhatsApp marketing?
questions.help: Native in Shopify Messaging.

questions.text: Which product reviews app is used or preferred?
questions.help: Product reviews need an app.

Which affiliate platform, if any?

questions.text: Are affiliate and influencer sales tracked via discount codes, UTM parameters, or both?
Which discount types are used?
Which discounts must combine on one order?
questions.help: Shopify combines product, order and shipping discounts natively (up to 5 codes plus 1 shipping code, and up to 25 automatic discounts). Custom logic needs a discount function.

native.plan_note: Up to 5 codes + 1 shipping code; 25 automatic discounts

native.feature: Several product discounts on the same line item
native.plan_note: Plan requirement to recheck after Spring '26

questions.text: Are coupon codes single-use, multi-use, or bulk-generated?
Must codes be brand-named (e.g. WELCOME20)?
Do codes need minimum order values or quantities?
Do codes expire on a fixed date, a rolling period, or never?
How are codes distributed (email, SMS, print, influencers)?
Do promotions differ by market, customer segment, sales channel or B2B company?
Are gift cards sold as a product?
questions.help: Gift cards are native: digital cards by email, physical cards on POS; they never expire by default. Also covers gift cards accepted at checkout.

questions.text: Are gift cards issued as rewards or compensation?
Digital gift cards, physical, or both?
Must gift cards expire?
Are promotions triggered from email or SMS campaigns?
Does each campaign need its own landing page?
Are countdown timers or urgency elements needed?
questions.help: Countdown timers need an app or theme work.

questions.text: Do you run scheduled drops or flash sales with high traffic?
questions.help: Scheduled theme and checkout changes are native (Rollouts).

questions.text: Do you want your products to be found and bought inside AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Google AI or Copilot?
questions.help: AI assistants are becoming a shopping channel. Shopify already switches eligible stores on by default, so this is a decision to confirm or reverse, not one to postpone.

native.feature: Agentic storefronts (active by default for eligible stores)

teach.why: This decides whether a new sales channel is open or closed. Shopify enrols eligible stores automatically, so doing nothing is itself a decision — the channel is on.

options.pros: Reaches shoppers who start in an assistant instead of a search engine; no build work — Shopify feeds the catalogue
options.cons: Less control over presentation; the assistant owns the conversation; customer data is shared when checkout happens inside it

options.pros: Full control of the journey and the data
options.cons: Invisible where a growing share of product research starts; competitors listed instead

teach.limits: Eligibility is decided by Shopify: Starter plan or higher, not a private store, and some channels only for merchants selling to US buyers. Business-to-business products are excluded automatically.

questions.text: Should Shopify enrol you automatically in new AI channels as they appear, or do you want to approve each one?
questions.help: The default setting also enrols you in channels that do not exist yet.

native.feature: Agentic channel management (Shopify-managed or per channel)

teach.why: AI channels are being added regularly. This decides whether the brand appears in a new one automatically, or only after your review.

options.pros: No admin work; the brand is present as new channels launch
options.cons: The brand can appear in a channel nobody reviewed, with terms and data sharing accepted in advance

options.pros: Brand, legal and data review before each launch
options.cons: Someone must own the review; the brand is late to new channels

teach.limits: The default is Shopify-managed enrolment, with catalogue access and checkout inside the assistant switched on.

questions.text: Should shoppers be able to pay inside the AI assistant, or should they come to your store to check out?
questions.help: Paying in the assistant converts better; sending them to your store keeps the full journey, the upsells and the analytics.

native.plan_note: Per channel; ChatGPT is referral only

teach.why: This is the commercial trade-off of the channel: conversion against ownership of the customer journey and the data.

options.pros: Fewer steps, so better conversion from an assistant conversation
options.cons: Your storefront, upsells and analytics are skipped; the channel receives the customer's name, e-mail, phone and address

options.pros: You keep merchandising, upsells, tracking and the customer relationship
options.cons: More steps between intent and purchase

teach.limits: ChatGPT always sends shoppers to your checkout; other channels can be set per channel.

questions.text: Do you sell to customers in the United States?
questions.help: Some AI channels are only open to merchants selling to US buyers, wherever the business is based.

native.plan_note: Starter plan or higher; some channels need US buyers

teach.why: It decides which AI channels are available at all, so it decides whether this section matters for launch.
teach.limits: ChatGPT and Copilot need US buyers; Google's AI channels are limited to selected US-based shops. A European merchant selling only in Europe may not be eligible today.

questions.text: Who can accept Shopify's additional terms for selling through AI channels?
questions.help: Selling through these channels requires accepting separate terms — usually legal or procurement, not the ecommerce team.

teach.why: The channel cannot go live until someone with authority accepts separate terms. Naming that person early avoids a launch-week block.
teach.limits: The supplemental terms are accepted in the Shopify admin, and acceptance covers the channels the store is enrolled in.

questions.text: Are you comfortable sharing the customer's name, e-mail, phone and address with an AI channel when they buy inside it?
questions.help: This is a data-protection decision. Under GDPR it usually needs a documented review before launch.

native.feature: Customer data shared with agentic channels on direct checkout

teach.why: Checkout inside the assistant means order data reaches a third party. It is the same kind of decision as adding a new processor, and it belongs with the data-protection owner.

options.pros: Checkout inside the assistant stays available, with its conversion benefit
options.cons: A third party processes customer data; needs a record and probably a contract

options.pros: No new processor; simpler privacy position
options.cons: Checkout in the assistant must be switched off; the channel becomes referral only

teach.limits: The data is shared only for orders placed through direct checkout in the channel.

questions.text: How complete is your product data — titles, images, prices, descriptions and variants?
questions.help: AI channels only list products whose data is complete. Gaps make products invisible rather than badly presented.

teach.why: Product-data quality decides visibility in AI channels, and it is the cheapest thing to fix before launch.
teach.limits: A product needs a title, at least one image, a price above zero, an identifiable URL and publication to the online store. Eligibility is reviewed over time, not only once.

questions.text: Is important product information kept in custom fields, separate records or inside the product title (for example “Steel 40mm — Automatic”)?
questions.help: Data that lives in custom fields or in the title needs mapping before AI channels can read it.

teach.why: It decides whether there is a data workstream. Attributes that matter commercially — material, size, movement — are often in custom fields or packed into titles, where an assistant cannot read them reliably.
teach.limits: Shopify supports mapping custom fields and title patterns into the catalogue it sends to AI channels; that mapping is work to plan.

questions.text: Should AI crawlers be allowed, restricted or blocked on your website?
questions.help: Blocking crawlers does not remove your products from AI shopping channels; it only affects what they read from your public site.

teach.why: Brands often want to block AI crawlers to protect content, then find their products still appear — the two routes are separate.

options.pros: Editorial content, guides and brand story can be cited by assistants
options.cons: Content can be summarised without a visit to the site

options.pros: Protects editorial content and images from open-web crawling
options.cons: No effect on the product data Shopify sends to AI channels; can reduce visibility in AI answers

teach.limits: Crawler rules are advisory and are set in the theme; they do not stop the Shopify product feed.

questions.text: Do you want to control the answers AI assistants give about shipping, returns and sizing?
questions.help: Shopify has a free app that publishes your FAQs for assistants and logs what shoppers ask.

teach.why: Assistants answer service questions whether or not you supply the answers. Publishing them keeps the answers right and shows what customers actually ask.
teach.limits: The FAQ content is a free Shopify app; the query log shows what shoppers asked about the store.

questions.text: Do you plan to offer your own AI shopping assistant, or connect the store to agent platforms yourself?
questions.help: Parts of this are still early access at Shopify, so treat it as exploration rather than fixed scope.

native.feature: Universal Commerce Protocol and agent interfaces
native.plan_note: Universal Cart API is early access

teach.why: It separates “be present where assistants already are” from “build your own assistant”. The second is a project in its own right and partly on pre-release technology.
teach.limits: Shopify publishes an open protocol and store endpoints for agents; the cart part is early access, and plan requirements are not documented yet.

questions.text: Which Shopify AI tools do you want your team to use in day-to-day work?
questions.help: These are back-office tools for your team, not customer-facing.

native.plan_note: Included; features and limits vary by plan
Shopify or Advanced plan; under 200,000 products

teach.why: It separates customer-facing AI from staff productivity, and flags a training and governance need rather than a build.
teach.limits: The assistant and content tools are included in the plans, with limits varying by plan; better on-site search needs a specific plan and a catalogue under 200,000 products.

questions.text: Existing Shopify store: what do the agentic sales-channel settings show today (Sales channels → Agentic)?
questions.help: Check the admin with the client: enrolment mode, which channels are on, and whether checkout inside the assistant is enabled.

teach.why: On an existing store the settings are already live, so the consultant reads the current state instead of asking the client to imagine it.
teach.limits: Turning enrolment off can take up to seven days to take effect in some channels.

questions.text: List every system that exchanges product, inventory, order, customer or financial data with the store. For each: system, category, direction, data objects, frequency, connector (native app / iPaaS / custom / none), owner, status.
questions.help: Typical ownership: the PIM supplies products, attributes and translations; the ERP supplies prices (including B2B catalogs), inventory per location and order status.

native.feature: Admin API, bulk operations and webhooks
